description: Re-optimize the LOW-RANK routing + k-selection now that brief-24's split back-transform made the k<=448 megakernel INNER solve ~1.2-1.5x cheaper (shapes 3/8/12 already benefit). The cheaper inner solve CHANGES the k-vs-cost economics that brief-16 tuned under the OLD (slower) inner solve, opening levers brief-16 could not reach: (1) SHAPE 4 (dense1024 cond2, currently low-rank k=608 with its inner k-by-k eigh on cuSOLVER because k>448): its PR-probe effective rank is only ~47, so test whether a SMALLER k<=448 (e.g. 384/416/448) + power=1 or 2 still passes the residual gate -- if so its inner solve moves from cuSOLVER onto the fast split-megakernel (the k<=448 path), a direct speedup on a 76ms shape. (2) SHAPE 10 (nearrank1024 k=768, exact rank 3n/4): k is forced to 768 (brief-7: k below exact rank -> under-resolved -> fallback), but test whether a TWO-STAGE low-rank (project to k=768 dominant, then the k=768 inner block itself solved by a NESTED low-rank since nearrank's tail is ~1e-6) could shrink the inner work. (3) With the cheaper inner solve, the low-rank path can afford MORE power iterations (power=2) for better subspace accuracy -> lower fallback rate -> re-sweep the PR bands to route any dense n=512/1024 shapes currently just outside the bands (brief-7's _LOWRANK_BANDS) that now clear the gate. (4) Re-sweep k DOWNWARD on the already-won low-rank shapes 3/8/12 (smaller k = smaller complement + cheaper CQR2 + cheaper inner) to find the new accuracy-speed optimum under the split back-transform. PURE-TORCH ONLY (routing table + k constants + power counts; NO nvcc / no kernel edits) -- GPU-light amid SEVERE build-lock contention (brief-25 saw a 1154s wait). Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback is the correctness floor so any under-resolved k falls back safely (never regresses, only wins where it clears the gate faster). Forks best 391107f7; distinct from brief-25 (which edits the megakernel tridiag) -- this only touches the Python routing/k/power. no 'stream' substring; verify 39/39 + quiet re-bench beats 36398.

Both downward (t2, needs costly p2) and upward (t4, orth ceiling) k re-sweeps refuted -> parent k values are the measured optimum.

ALL FOUR BRIEF LEVERS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT (fallback-rate probes + benchmarks):
L1 shape4 k<=448: eig gate needs k>=608. Probe: k=448 p1/p2 -> 100% fallback, eig 5.35e-2/5.25e-2 vs gate 1.83e-2; k=512 3.2e-2; k=576 1.9e-2 (11.7% fb); k=608 1.57e-2 (0% fb). The 'effective rank ~47' is optimistic -- the dense1024 inner block (PR~110) has only 98.19% l1-energy in top-448 dims, needs ~578. Firmly stuck on cuSOLVER inner (k>448 overflows the mega SMEM cap).
L2 shape10 nested: the k=768 inner block is NEARLY FLAT (PR~326, |eig| ratio only 10x, spectrum [0.1,1.0], 82% energy in top-448) -> NOT low-rank-nestable. nearrank's ~1e-6 tail is in the DROPPED complement, not the dominant block.
L3 power=2 -> route more: power=2 reduces fallback NOWHERE that matters (shapes 4/10/12 already 0-fb at p1; shape12 100% fb below k=384 even at p3; mixed512/1024 orth 4.3/9.0 regardless of power). And power=2 COSTS ~12-14% at b640 (t1 shape8 93324->105038; t2 shape3 81039->92692) -- the extra A@Qd + CQR2 pass at b640 far exceeds the fallbacks it removes.
L4 downward/upward k on 3/8/12: DOWNWARD needs power=2 (too costly, t2); shape12 can't drop below 384 even at p3 (eig gate). UPWARD hits a newly-measured MEGA-INNER ORTH CEILING ~k=384 (t4 shape3 k=416 -> 271509us +235%): the FP16 megakernel inner solve's eigenvector orthogonality degrades sharply with block size (k=352 orth 7.9e-3 / k=384 1.2e-2 / k=400 0.78 / k=416 2.1) while eig keeps improving -> Vd=Qd@G loses orthonormality -> orth gate -> mass fallback. shapes 3(k352)/8(k384)/12(k384) sit right at this ceiling.

KEY NEW FINDING for follow-up steering: the split-mega inner solve has a hard ORTH ceiling ~k=384 -- so raising the low-rank k is blocked NOT by eig accuracy but by the megakernel's FP16 orthogonality. If brief-25's tridiag work (or an FP32/BF16-storage megakernel variant) RAISED that orth ceiling, shapes 3/8/12 could take LARGER k (smaller complement -> cheaper CQR2/AVc) AND shapes 4/10's inner blocks could move off cuSOLVER -- the single biggest unlocked lever on the low-rank shapes.
